title: Choose a service model from constraints
summary: Classify eight original workload requirements. The three real service-model choices are intentional; unrelated labels are not added as artificial wrong options.

kernel-control.clue: The workload must install a custom guest-kernel extension and the team will maintain that operating system. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

managed-web-runtime.clue: The team supplies a web app’s source; the host maintains its supported runtime and operating system. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

finished-mail.clue: Employees use a complete vendor-operated mail application and only configure their accounts. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

os-maintenance.clue: A migration keeps customer authority to install and schedule guest-OS updates on rented machines. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

managed-database.clue: Developers create schemas and queries on a managed database while its provider operates the underlying platform. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

finished-expenses.clue: Finance configures an existing vendor-maintained expense application; it does not deploy the application’s code. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

legacy-os.clue: An unchanged legacy workload must keep control over its guest OS and system-level configuration after moving to rented compute. Choose the service-model abbreviation.

app-development.clue: Developers build a custom application on a provider-maintained application platform rather than maintaining its servers. Choose the service-model abbreviation.
